last_3_hypotheses: Longer interaction horizons in iterated PD raise cooperation rates because the shadow of the future grows and the LLM weights long-run mutual cooperation above short-run defection benefit.

proposed_hypothesis_text: Longer interaction horizons in iterated PD increase the probability of mutual-defection lock-in once defection has occurred, because the LLM treats the long horizon as evidence that the relationship is already broken and continues to defect rather than risk being re-exploited.
rationale: Both hypotheses make claims about "long horizon" and PD cooperation, but the claims are opposite in direction and target different conditional regimes. The first says long horizon → more cooperation (no prior defection). The proposed says long horizon → more lock-in (conditional on a prior defection). These are not duplicates; they could even be reconciled as the same model's behavior in different states. A meta-reviewer relying on keyword similarity would false-flag.
